abstract: this memo specifies version 2 of the internet group management protocol (igmp), an internet standard protocol used by hosts to report their multicast group memberships to an adjacent multicast router. this memo obsoletes rfc 1112 (igmpv1).
changes from igmpv1: the igmpv1 'version' and 'type' fields are combined into a single 'type' field.
a new igmp type is assigned to version 2 membership report messages, allowing differentiation between igmpv1 and igmpv2 host report messages.
a new igmp type is created for the igmpv2 leave group message.
the membership query message is changed so that a previously unused field contains a new value, the max response time.
a querier election mechanism is standardized in igmpv2, unlike in igmpv1 which left the election up to the multicast routing protocol.
the igmpv2 spec relaxes the requirements on validity-checking for membership queries and membership reports.
the igmpv2 spec requires the presence of the ip router alert option [rfc 2113] in all packets described in this memo.
security considerations: a forged query message can cause querier duties to be assigned to the forger, potentially disrupting multicast traffic.
forged report messages can cause multicast routers to incorrectly believe there are group members on a subnet, leading to inefficient multicast routing.
forged version 1 report messages may put a router into a 'version 1 members present' state, causing it to ignore leave messages and potentially disrupt multicast traffic.
forged leave messages can cause unnecessary group-specific queries and extra processing.
defenses against forged messages include ignoring messages from unknown subnets and requiring router alert options for certain message types.
